provenance.paper_title: PEAM: Parametric Embodied Agent Memory through Contrastive Internalization of Experience in Minecraft

representation_paths.memory_component: per-category MoE-LoRA adapter bank over the multimodal fast module

evidence.paraphrase: Experience is internalized into a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts LoRA over a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct backbone with physically isolated per-category adapters for {craft, gather, combat}; consolidation updates only the category-specific adapter parameters via a joint behavioral-cloning plus PEAM-DPO contrastive objective on success and failure-correction pairs. The stored memory is the adapter weights themselves; no source trajectory is recoverable from them.

At execution time a task is routed to its category adapter and the fast path emits the consolidated skill reflexively from the visually conditioned parametric module; the slow LLM is invoked only when verification fails. Activation of memory is thus parametric rather than by explicit lookup.

representation_paths.memory_component: external episodic store of successful and failure-correction trajectories

evidence.paraphrase: An external episodic store stages tuples (task, skill category, executed trajectory, outcome) accumulated during live agent execution. Entries are executable JavaScript action code plus a discrete pre-action state vector (inventory composition, biome identity, time-of-day bucket, bot location); candidates are selected for consolidation by matching that state vector and by a Parameterization Worthiness score over cost saving, cross-context stability, redundancy, and interference. Raw visual observations are not retained, so the perceptual source is not recoverable.

During the agent's live Minecraft operation, a scale-free statistical trigger compares each skill's recent failure rate against its own historical baseline and, when the criterion fires, runs a gradient update of the category adapter over the staged trajectories. The parametric memory content therefore changes at deployment time; the trigger rule and the PV selection formula that govern the update are fixed.

Batches of concrete staged trajectories, including failure-correction contrasts, are abstracted into reusable parametric skills inside the adapter bank, replacing inference-time retrieval of individual episodes; later tasks in the same category reuse the abstracted skill.

derived.hybrid_relation: The explicit episodic trajectory store and the parametric adapter bank form one deliberate pipeline: staged symbolic trajectories are selected and consolidated into the parametric memory that then drives the fast execution path.

adjudication_notes: T3 explicitly rejected. Consolidation is triggered by deployment failure statistics (Section 3.4, Algorithm 1 lines 18-24) and persistently changes a reusable artifact, but the artifact changed is the parametric memory content (the adapters) and the staged episodic entries, not a memory write, maintenance, or retrieval policy. The write policy (Parameterization Worthiness score, Equation 3) and the maintenance policy (self-triggered consolidation criterion, Equation 4) are fixed formulas throughout deployment. Per the guide, feedback that changes only memory content or fixed per-item statistics is T2.

Residual uncertainty: the paper's own evaluation runs the agent in episodic task rollouts, so the boundary between 'deployment' and an offline consolidation cycle is described inconsistently (Section 3.4 calls consolidation decoupled/batched, while Algorithm 1 places it inside the per-task execution loop). The tier assignment does not depend on this, since either reading yields at most T2.
